title: Shoulder reduction under procedural sedation
stem: Resus 4. Mr Lui, 17, dislocated his left shoulder falling while skateboarding. The X-ray confirms an anterior dislocation without fracture. Consent has been obtained. Demonstrate how you would reduce it under procedural sedation.
notes:
Checked against RCEM/RCoA 'Safe sedation of adults in the ED' (2012, RCEM 2019 update), and evidence on reduction techniques (Cunningham, external rotation, FARES, Spaso, Milch, Kocher).

Safety: resus bay, two clinicians (a sedationist separate from the person reducing), monitoring (SpO2, ECG, NIBP, capnography), oxygen, suction, airway kit, reversal agents. Neurovascular check before (axillary nerve badge sensation and deltoid; radial, median, ulnar motor; radial pulse) and after. Sedation: titrate, e.g. midazolam 0.02–0.1 mg/kg with fentanyl 0.5–1 microgram/kg, or propofol, or ketamine 1–2 mg/kg; aim for deep enough relaxation (your notes use the modified Ramsay score 4–5). Many dislocations reduce without sedation (Cunningham, external rotation), which avoids sedation risk.

Kocher's method carries a higher risk of fracture and nerve injury (your notes say so). After reduction: X-ray, sling, recovery observation until the discharge criteria are met, written advice. Your notes on doses, techniques and signs of reduction match this.

steps.label: Set up
steps.hint: Monitoring with capnography, oxygen, suction, airway kit, reversal agents, IV access, separate sedationist.

opts.t: SpO2, ECG, NIBP and capnography on
Oxygen, suction, bag-valve-mask and airway adjuncts at the bedside
Naloxone and flumazenil drawn up nearby
IV cannula in the other arm
Dr Kwan runs the sedation; I do the reduction

steps.label: Neurovascular check
steps.hint: Axillary, radial, median, ulnar, radial pulse.

Before.t: Sensation over the regimental badge area
Before.mark: Checks the axillary nerve before reduction

Before.t: Wrist extension, finger flexion, finger abduction
Before.mark: Checks radial, median and ulnar motor function

steps.label: Sedate and reduce
steps.hint: Titrate sedation, one gentle technique, feel for the clunk, re-examine.

opts.t: Fentanyl 1 microgram/kg, then midazolam titrated in small doses
Wait for adequate sedation (drowsy, relaxed, responds to a firm tap)
External rotation technique: elbow at 90° by the side, slowly externally rotate
Feel the clunk; the contour of the shoulder returns
opts.r: A soft clunk. The shoulder is round again.

opts.t: Re-check nerves and pulse; sling; post-reduction X-ray
opts.mark: Post-reduction neurovascular check, sling and X-ray

opts.t: Observe until awake and discharge criteria met

opts.r: Higher fracture and nerve injury rates; use gentler techniques first.

opts.t: The sedationist leaves to help reduce
opts.r: The sedationist must watch the airway throughout.

wrong: Measures the depth of sedation directly and continuously
It is required for billing the procedure

qs.q: Which nerve to check before and after?
A technique that often works without sedation?

badge.name: Clunk
badge.flavor: Two doctors, capnography, gentle rotation, nerves checked twice.

cards.q: Minimum staff for ED procedural sedation?
options: A sedationist plus a separate operator
A nurse giving the drugs alone
cards.why: The sedationist focuses on the airway.

options: Traction with vertical oscillation while abducting
Foot in the axilla with steady traction
Hanging weights from the wrist for 30 minutes

cards.q: After reduction, the X-ray looks for…
options: Congruent joint and fractures (Hill-Sachs, Bankart, greater tuberosity)
Lung pathology such as a pneumothorax
Asleep, rouses to a loud voice or tap
Unresponsive, even to a firm trapezius squeeze
cards.why: Target for reduction per your notes.
